title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection

problem.summary: DETR is the first fully end-to-end detector but converges very slowly (500 epochs on COCO) and handles small objects poorly, because Transformer attention over image feature maps is quadratic in pixel count and starts near-uniform.
statements: DETR needs roughly 10 to 20 times more training epochs to converge than Faster R-CNN on COCO.
High-resolution feature maps needed for small objects lead to unacceptable complexity for DETR's self-attention.
Transformer attention casts nearly uniform weights at initialization, so long training schedules are required before attention focuses on sparse meaningful locations.

evidence.quote: However, it suffers from slow convergence and limited feature spatial resolution, due to the limitation of Transformer attention modules in processing image feature maps.
For example, on the COCO (Lin et al., 2014) benchmark, DETR needs 500 epochs to converge, which is around 10 to 20 times slower than Faster R-CNN (Ren et al., 2015).
DETR delivers relatively low performance at detecting small objects.

background.summary: The work builds on DETR (Transformer encoder-decoder with Hungarian set prediction), deformable convolution, and multi-scale feature pyramids (FPN and variants). The gap claimed is that prior efficient-attention designs are limited to fixed sparse patterns and that DETR's attention on feature maps is both slow to train and quadratic in spatial size.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: base end-to-end detector whose attention modules are replaced
relatedWork.quote: DETR has been recently proposed to eliminate the need for many hand-designed components in object detection while demonstrating good performance.

relatedWork.name: Deformable Convolution
relatedWork.relation: inspiration for sparse spatial sampling in the proposed attention
relatedWork.quote: In the image domain, deformable convolution (Dai et al., 2017) is of a powerful and efficient mechanism to attend to sparse spatial locations.

relatedWork.name: FPN
relatedWork.relation: prior multi-scale feature fusion that the proposed module makes unnecessary
relatedWork.quote: As one of the pioneering works, FPN (Lin et al., 2017a) proposes a top-down path to combine multi-scale features.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.quote: which is around 10 to 20 times slower than Faster R-CNN (Ren et al., 2015)

evidence.quote: Modern object detectors employ many hand-crafted components (Liu et al., 2020), e.g., anchor generation, rule-based training target assignment, non-maximum suppression (NMS) post-processing.
On the other hand, the attention weights computation in Transformer encoder is of quadratic computation w.r.t. pixel numbers.

solution.summary: Deformable DETR replaces the Transformer attention modules that process feature maps with multi-scale deformable attention, which samples a small set of key points around a reference point from multi-scale feature maps, giving linear complexity and 10x faster convergence; iterative box refinement and a two-stage variant further raise accuracy.
solution.approach: Attend only to a small fixed set of learned sampling locations around a reference point (deformable style) instead of all pixels, aggregated across four feature levels inside a DETR encoder-decoder.
components: multi-scale deformable attention module (default M = 8 heads, K = 4 sampling points)
deformable Transformer encoder over C3-C6 multi-scale feature maps without FPN
decoder cross-attention replaced by multi-scale deformable attention, self-attention unchanged
object-query reference points predicted via linear projection and sigmoid
box prediction as relative offsets to the reference point
iterative bounding box refinement across decoder layers
two-stage variant: encoder-only proposals fed back as object queries, no NMS
Focal Loss classification with 300 object queries

evidence.quote: we proposed Deformable DETR, whose attention modules only attend to a small set of key sampling points around a reference.
the deformable attention module only attends to a small set of key sampling points around a reference point, regardless of the spatial size of the feature maps, as shown in Fig. 2.
We replace the Transformer attention modules processing feature maps in DETR with the proposed multi-scale deformable attention module.
each decoder layer refines the bounding boxes based on the predictions from the previous layer.

experiments.summary: Evaluation is on COCO 2017: comparison against DETR on the val set including convergence curves and runtime, ablations of the deformable attention design choices, and comparison with state-of-the-art detectors on test-dev.

benchmarks.split: val, two-stage Deformable DETR with iterative refinement, 50 epochs

evidence.quote: Compared with DETR, Deformable DETR can achieve better performance (especially on small objects) with 10× less training epochs.
With ResNet-101 and ResNeXt-101 (Xie et al., 2017), our method achieves 48.7 AP and 49.0 AP without bells and whistles, respectively.

limitations.summary: Deformable attention still relies on unordered memory access, so it remains slightly slower than plain convolution, and its runtime is about 25% slower than Faster R-CNN + FPN; the strongest numbers also depend on the iterative-refinement/two-stage variants and test-time augmentation.
items: Deformable attention is still slightly slower than traditional convolution because of unordered memory access.
Inference is about 25% slower than Faster R-CNN + FPN despite on-par FLOPs.
Best test-dev results (52.3 AP) require test-time augmentation; base ResNet-50 model reaches 46.9 AP.
Only cross-attention is deformable; decoder self-attention is left unchanged.

evidence.quote: Our proposed deformable attention can mitigate this issue, at the cost of unordered memory access.
But the runtime speed is much faster (1.6×) than DETR-DC5, and is just 25% slower than Faster R-CNN + FPN.

futureDirections.direction: Explore further interesting and practical variants of end-to-end object detectors built on Deformable DETR.
futureDirections.quote: It enables us to explore more interesting and practical variants of end-to-end object detectors.

futureDirections.direction: Use the fast-converging, efficient design as a basis for new end-to-end detection research.
futureDirections.quote: We hope our work opens up new possibilities in exploring end-to-end object detection.

equations.name: Multi-head attention
equations.expr: MultiHeadAttn(z_q, x) = sum_m W_m [ sum_k A_mqk W'_m x_k ]

equations.name: Deformable attention
equations.expr: DeformAttn(z_q, p_q, x) = sum_m W_m [ sum_k A_mqk W'_m x(p_q + Delta_p_mqk) ]

equations.name: Multi-scale deformable attention
equations.expr: MSDeformAttn(z_q, p_q, {x_l}) = sum_m W_m [ sum_l sum_k A_mlqk W'_m x^l(phi_l(p_q) + Delta_p_mlqk) ]

equations.name: Deformable attention complexity
equations.expr: O(2 N_q C^2 + min(HW C^2, N_q K C^2))

deploymentClaims: 19 FPS inference on an NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU (Table 1)
1.6x faster runtime than DETR-DC5 at on-par FLOPs

evidence.quote: Run time is evaluated on NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU.
But the runtime speed is much faster (1.6×) than DETR-DC5, and is just 25% slower than Faster R-CNN + FPN.
